name: recovery-d-002
prompt:
Create ORIGINAL FORMA fitness-manual artwork, landscape1536x1024, exactly THREE columns and TWO rows, SIX separate equal panels512x512 on pure white. Generous white gutters no borders. One full adult athlete per cell, fully clothed charcoal/gray fitness clothing with tiny lime accent; charcoal accurate equipment, subtle shadow. Correct plausible anatomy two arms/two legs. ALL complete figures, equipment and supporting surfaces fit each512x512cell with white margins. No words letters logos labels arrows ghost poses. Detail hand grip, foot contact and equipment. Show only described representative phase. Never exchange cable/band, bench, grip or knee depth.
Row 1 column 1: One-Arm Kettlebell Push Press. EXACT POSE: One kettlebell overhead in one hand at push-press FINISH: athlete standing upright, both knees and hips straight, working elbow straight locked above shoulder, free arm at side, feet shoulder width. Source guide: Hold a kettlebell by the handle. Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder by extending through the legs and hips as you pull the kettlebell towards your shoulder. Rotate your wrist as you do so, so that the palm faces forward. This will be your starting position.

Dip your body by bending the knees, keeping your torso upright.

Immediately reverse direction, driving through the heels, in essence jumping to create momentum. As you do so, press the kettlebell overhead to lockout by extending the arms, using your body's momentum to move the weight. Lower the weight to perform the next repetition.

Row 1 column 2: One-Arm Side Deadlift. EXACT POSE: Suitcase-style one-arm BARBELL deadlift lockout: athlete standing upright with loaded barbell running FRONT TO BACK beside right leg (perpendicular to shoulder line). Single hand grips CENTER shaft beside hip, straight elbow. Entire bar lies beside body not across thighs. Perspective view shows both plates. Source guide: Stand to the side of a barbell next to its center. Bend your knees and lower your body until you are able to reach the barbell.

Grasp the bar as if you were grabbing a briefcase (palms facing you since the bar is sideways). You may need a wrist wrap if you are using a significant amount of weight. This is your starting position.

Use your legs to help lift the barbell up while exhaling. Your arms should extend fully as bring the barbell up until you are in a standing position.

Slowly bring the barbell back down while inhaling. Tip: Make sure to bend your knees while lowering the weight to avoid any injury from occurring.

Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

Switch arms and repeat the movement.

Row 1 column 3: Open Palm Kettlebell Clean. EXACT POSE: Open-palm kettlebell clean catch: athlete upright, bell BALL rests in both OPEN cupped palms at upper chest, handle pointing upward free and untouched. Fingers under spherical bell body, two hands fully visible. Source guide: Place one kettlebell between your feet. Clean the kettlebell by extending through the legs and hips as you raise the kettlebell towards your shoulders.

Release the kettlebell as it comes up, and let it flip so that the ball of the kettlebell lands in the palms of your hands.

Release the kettlebell out in front of you and catch the handle with both hands. Lower the kettlebell to the starting position and repeat.

Row 2 column 1: Palms-Up Barbell Wrist Curl Over A Bench. EXACT POSE: Kneeling palms-UP barbell wrist curl over flat bench: both forearms resting horizontal on bench, wrists beyond edge. Palms face ceiling under bar, fingers curl around bar from underneath; supination unmistakable, no upper-arm curl. Source guide: Start out by placing a barbell on one side of a flat bench.

Kneel down on both of your knees so that your body is facing the flat bench.

Use your arms to grab the barbell with a supinated grip (palms up) and bring them up so that your forearms are resting against the flat bench. Your wrists should be hanging over the edge.

Start out by curling your wrist upwards and exhaling.

Slowly lower your wrists back down to the starting position while inhaling.

Your forearms should be stationary as your wrist is the only movement needed to perform this exercise.

Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

Row 2 column 2: Palms-Up Dumbbell Wrist Curl Over A Bench. EXACT POSE: Kneeling palms-UP two dumbbell wrist curl: both forearms flat horizontal on bench, wrists hanging beyond edge. Open palm surfaces face ceiling; dumbbells supported from underneath with fingers curled, no pronated knuckles-on-top. Source guide: Start out by placing two dumbbells on one side of a flat bench.

Kneel down on both of your knees so that your body is facing the flat bench.

Use your arms to grab both of the dumbbells with a supinated grip (palms up) and bring them up so that your forearms are resting against the flat bench. Your wrists should be hanging over the edge.

Start out by curling your wrist upwards and exhaling.

Slowly lower your wrists back down to the starting position while inhaling. Make sure to inhale during this part of the exercise.

Your forearms should be stationary as your wrist is the only movement needed to perform this exercise.

Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

Row 2 column 3: Pause Hack Squats. EXACT POSE: Paused hack squat on compact angled hack-squat sled machine: back flat on sled pad, shoulder pads resting shoulders, feet on angled footplate; bottom squat knees bent, hands on handles. Full machine inside cell. Source guide: Hack Squats but with a 1-2s pause at the bottom of the movement. This makes sure that there is no more elastic energy stored in the muscles.
